name: Remote Browser

modes.label: Purchased browser-hour packs
modes.note: $4.90/20 hours; purchased in packs, not a promised continuous overage meter. Unspecified guest OS is not a selectable OS guarantee.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: 1 browser-hour/month; 1 viewer and profile; 1-day recording retention.

plans.name: Developer
plans.note: 30 included hours valued at pack rate; 3 viewers/browser,20 profiles,7-day recording retention. First month $.10 promotion.

features.ip_note: Provider-managed proxy egress (residential, mobile, datacenter; per-request rotation or sticky; country routing), proxy can be disabled, BYO HTTP/SOCKS5 proxy supported; no per-GB price published.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv 4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.
Each session is a Kubernetes pod, not a dedicated resource-guaranteed VM. Active browser-hour means alive runtime, not active CPU time.
Model the top-up as a 20-hour purchase block, not unlimited metered $.245/hour. Credit expiry, proxy bandwidth, CPU/RAM, CAPTCHA fee and storage GiB price not published.

OS (verified 2026-09-28, remote-browser.dev/architecture): 'Remote-browser runs on Kubernetes. Each session is a pod'; 'One Chromium per pod'. Sessions are Linux containers, so os = ['linux'] (a browser product, not a Linux machine you control).
SSH: sessions are Chromium pods reached over a CDP socket (remote-browser.dev/architecture, 2026-09-28); no shell/SSH access is offered. ssh = false.

Default session timeout is 5 minutes (integration env REMOTE_BROWSER_TIMEOUT_MINUTES=5; profile CDP URL '...&timeout=5'); browser-hours accrue until the idle-timeout controller kills the pod or the client terminates it, so every abandoned session carries up to ~5 billed minutes.

Hard caps, no overage meter: when included browser-hours run out, more runtime only comes from $4.90/20 h one-time packs ('Simple caps, no surprise bills'; billing integration has 'Plan-aware caps'). Bandwidth and recording bytes are metered per org and bandwidth is throttled per session/plan, but no price is published.

Homepage claims 'Real Chromium in 14 regions' (API region example 'fra1', default 'auto') but publishes no region list (features.regions left null). It also advertises Web Tasks (/v1/tasks), Custom Models routing and 'Remote-browser v3', none of which are in the pricing table; SSH access is mentioned but not documented (ssh=false kept).

fleet.notes: Runtime-hour top-ups do not raise concurrency; 50/300/1,000 increase route unverified. Viewer connection caps are separate.
